Pricing my homemade goodies is honestly my LEAST favorite thing to do. 😥🥹
I was debating between $2 and $3 per mini tart, and eventually decided on $3 each or a box of 4 for $11 which technically make them $2.75 Why? Because they're made from scratch, handmade one by one, and filled with delicious fillings that take extra time, ingredients, and effort 🩷
Some customers see the work that goes into them and think they're absolutely worth it, and that makes me so happy because they understand the love and effort behind every little tart 🥹🫶🏻
But then there are others who react with, “DAAAMN, $3?!” 😭😂 and then say, “I'll just take a cake pop instead!”
And honestly, that got me thinking...
My cake pops are also $3 each. They're handmade and made from scratch, too! But they're two completely different products, with different ingredients, preparation methods, and finishing touches. My tarts have their own dough and fillings, while cake pops have their own process, ingredients, and coating.

So why do we sometimes compare two completely different handmade products just because they have the same price? 🥹 I myself did!!

I completely understand that everyone has a budget, and not everyone will find the same things worth buying I also did it mantly times!. That's okay! You don't have to buy something just because I make it or X person make it🫶

But there's a difference between something not fitting your budget and assuming it's overpriced without considering what goes into making it.

Some bakers made me realize that Small homemade businesses aren't just selling ingredients. We're putting our time, effort, skills, and love into every single product. We also have packaging costs, supplies, and all the little expenses that customers don't always see.

And honestly, pricing our products shouldn't mean having to make everyone happy. Some people will think it's worth it, and others won't. That's perfectly fine!

As a small home baker, I'm still learning, growing, and figuring out pricing, and I know it's not always easy. I want my goodies to be affordable, but I also want to value my own work and make sure the time and effort I put into them are worth it 🥹💗

What do you think? Do you think people sometimes compare handmade products without considering the work that goes into each one? 👀💕

🧄🧀 CREAMY GARLIC PARMESAN DIPPED CHEESEBURGERS 🍔🤤

Juicy cheeseburgers dipped in a rich, creamy garlic Parmesan sauce… because regular cheeseburgers just aren’t enough 😍

INGREDIENTS :
 For the burgers: 
• 1 lb ground beef (80/20)
 • 4 brioche burger buns 
• 4 slices American cheese or provolone
 • Salt & black pepper 
• 1 tsp garlic powder 
• 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce (optional)

🧄 For the creamy garlic Parmesan sauce:
 • 2 tbsp butter
 • 5 garlic cloves, minced
 • 1 tbsp all-purpose flour 
• 1 cup heavy cream 
• ¾ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
 • ¼ tsp Italian seasoning 
• ¼ tsp paprika (optional) • Salt & black pepper to taste
 • 2–4 tbsp milk, as needed 
• Fresh parsley (optional)

INSTRUCTIONS :

1️⃣ Shape the ground beef into 4 patties. 
Season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.

2️⃣ Sear in a hot skillet for about 3–5 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Add the cheese during the last minute and cook until melted. Make sure the beef reaches 160°F internally.

3️⃣ In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Add the minced garlic and cook for 30–60 seconds until fragrant.

4️⃣ Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Slowly pour in the heavy cream, whisking until smooth.

5️⃣ Simmer gently for 2–4 minutes until slightly thickened. Lower the heat and stir in the Parmesan, Italian seasoning, paprika, salt, and pepper.

6️⃣ Add a little milk if needed until the sauce is smooth, creamy, and pourable.

7️⃣ Toast the brioche buns with a little butter until golden. Assemble your cheeseburgers with the cheesy patties.

8️⃣ THE BEST PART 🤤 Dip the burgers into that creamy garlic Parmesan sauce or generously pour it all over the top! Finish with fresh parsley and extra Parmesan.

🔥 Serve immediately with crispy fries or onion rings and EXTRA sauce for dipping!

Save this recipe for your next burger night! 🍔🧄🧀
